title: Customer Loss — Deep Dive & Counterfactual Playbook
body:
Purpose: A lightweight, investigation-first template for Customer Success teams to capture why a renewal was lost, what signals were missed, and concrete counterfactuals that could change outcomes next time. Use prior to QBRs and as inputs to playbook updates and CSM coaching.

Scope and when to use:
- Use for any lost or downgraded account where the committed ARR >= $25k or strategic impact is medium/high.
- Triage within 48–72 hours of contract lapsing or signed downgrade.

One-line summary (TL;DR):
- [Example: "Mid-market fintech ended contract after month-to-month use; primary driver: integration latency + product gaps vs competitor; sales pricing negotiation stalled."]

Customer profile:
- Company: [name]
- Segment: [AI-native / SaaS / Enterprise] 
- ARR at risk: [USD]
- Primary contact / champion: [name, title]
- Product usage snapshot: [weekly active seats, API calls/day, top features used]

Chronological timeline (minimal, fact-focused):
- T-90: [Sales upsell conversation, expectations set] 
- T-60: [Onboarding milestones missed / initial integration started] 
- T-30: [Support SLA breach, 3 outages recorded] 
- T-14: [Renewal negotiation begins; discount request submitted] 
- T-3: [Customer informs they will not renew; reason given] 
- T0: [Contract terminated / downgraded] 

Signals & evidence (logs, tickets, meetings):
- Product telemetry: [token latency percentiles, error rates, embedding QPS]
- Support tickets: [ticket IDs and summaries] 
- Account notes: [key Slack excerpts, emails, call recordings] 
- Quote / pricing: [final terms offered and comparator] 

Primary stated reasons (from customer) — quote verbatim where possible:
- Reason A: "..."
- Reason B: "..."
- Reason C: "..."

Root-cause hypotheses (ranked, with supporting evidence):
1) Technical / performance: [e.g., 95th pct latency on long conversations increased after model upgrade — link to dashboard]. Evidence: [metrics, tickets].
2) Product fit / missing features: [e.g., no structured output support for their sequence tagging]. Evidence: [feature request numbers, competitor features].
3) Commercial / pricing: [discount denied, procurement timing]. Evidence: [sales notes, final quote].
4) Relationship / communication: [missed QBRs, single point of contact replaced]. Evidence: [meeting misses, stakeholder change log].

Counterfactual scenarios — if X had been different, outcome might change. For each scenario include: "What would we do differently?", "Estimated effort", "Probability impact", "Owner & time horizon".
- CF1: Faster SLA response + targeted perf patch deployed within 7 days.
  - What: emergency perf patch + prioritized support rota.
  - Effort: engineering sprint (2 days), SRE on-call.
  - Impact: high (could prevent churn if performance was main driver).
  - Owner: eng-sre + CSM, horizon: 7–14 days.
- CF2: Short-term feature shim / integration adapter built to meet customer schema.
  - What: connector + mapping layer.
  - Effort: small eng ticket (1–2 sprints).
  - Impact: medium.
  - Owner: solutions-eng + PM.
- CF3: Structured commercial concession with success milestones (time-limited discount tied to SLOs).
  - What: limited-term credit and committed remediation plan.
  - Effort: legal + sales, low friction but needs cross-team signoff.
  - Impact: medium–high for price-sensitive accounts.

Counterfactual confidence & blocking assumptions: list assumptions that must hold for the CFs to have worked (e.g., ability to schedule eng resources within 7 days; customer willingness to run pilot; legal signoff for credits).

Immediate remediation & winback checklist (30/60/90 day roadmap):
- 0–7 days: Confirm termination reason in writing, collect final evidence bundle, exec brief prepared, triage board created.
- 7–30 days: Build and ship high-priority bugfix or perf mitigation; run joint success plan workshop; propose formal winback terms.
- 30–90 days: Offer pilot with SLA credits, monitor usage and sentiment weekly, update renewal tracker and QBR talking points.

Playbook changes (lessons to encode into CS practice):
- Add automated SLO alerts to early-warning dashboard and tie to CSM daily digest.
- For accounts >$25k ARR, require monthly technical QBR during onboarding quarter.
- Pricing: add a tactical 3-month "remediation credit" SKU for manageably fast concessions.
- Sales handoff: include 30-day technical readiness check before renewal window opens.

Owner assignments & follow-ups:
- Postmortem owner: [name] (deadline for final report: +14 days)
- Engineering lead for remediation: [name] (deliverable + ETA)
- Solutions-eng contact: [name] (connector work)
- Legal & finance: [name] (winback terms template)

Metrics to track (to measure if counterfactuals would have helped):
- Time to acknowledge SLA incident (hours)
- 95th percentile latency for impacted API endpoints
- Number of active seats / API calls in 30 days after proposed remediation
- Renewal conversion rate for accounts with remediations applied

Communication templates (copy/paste):
- Email to exec sponsor: "We take full ownership of the outage that impacted X. Here is what we did and the path to ensure this won’t repeat..."
- Winback offer template: "We understand the impact you saw. We propose a short-term remediation plan + X credits if milestones met..."

Open questions / notes to self:
- Did we track internal prioritization requests (support -> eng) with JIRA IDs? If not, add to evidence.
- Is there a legal restriction on crediting usage retroactively?

Appendix (where to store evidence):
- Slack thread IDs, Support ticket IDs, Recording links, Dashboard snapshots.
- Recommended tags for filing: churn-YYYY, loss-reason-performance, playbook-update-needed.

How this ties to QBRs and renewal tracker:
- Inject the top 2 findings into next QBR template under "Risks & mitigations".
- In renewal tracker, add flag: "remediation in process" and next checkpoint date.

Quick checklist for finalizing this doc (CS owner to complete):
- [ ] Attach call recording + timestamped notes
- [ ] Link to SLO dashboard snapshots
- [ ] Confirm final commercial terms and attach signed doc
- [ ] Share with sales and eng leads for feedback

Notes on tone / usage: Keep this doc concise and evidence-driven. Avoid speculation in the timeline — keep conjecture in the counterfactuals section only. Use this as the canonical loss file for the account and feed sanitized lessons into the public playbook.
